items.answer: the plain average of the four values
accepted: the average of the four value vectors
the mean of the four value vectors
an equally weighted average of the values
the sum of the values divided by four
items.rationale: Equal scores give equal softmax weights of 0.25 each, so the output is the unweighted mean of the four values. An answer naming a single value shows M4 (attention as a hard pick); 'the sum of the values' without dividing is partial.

Dot products of independent unit-variance components have variance d_k, so with d_k = 1024 scores spread to about plus or minus 32; softmax saturates to nearly one-hot and its gradients become extremely small (Vaswani et al., 3.2.1).

The causal mask sets scores for positions after 3 to minus infinity, so their weights are exactly 0; tokens 1, 2 and 3 keep positive weights. An answer of 5 ignores the mask (M1); an answer of 2 forgets that a token attends to itself.
QK^T is n by n, so going to 2n gives (2n)^2 = 4n^2 entries: four times as many. This is the O(n^2 d) cost per layer.

items.answer: French, because the queries come from the decoder, which produces the French output
accepted: French, the decoder supplies the queries
French, since queries come from the decoder
the French sentence, from the decoder
items.rationale: In encoder-decoder attention the queries come from the previous decoder layer and the keys and values from the encoder output (Vaswani et al., 3.2.3); the decoder writes French. 'French' with no reason or a wrong reason is partial; 'English' swaps the roles of encoder and decoder.

0.5 * [2, 4] + 0.5 * [6, 0] + 0 * [100, 100] = [1, 2] + [3, 0] = [4, 2]. Option b picks one value outright (M4), c averages all three values ignoring the weights, and d adds the values without the weights.
